day.readme: An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company, powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

day.readme: Hunt down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks    •       •    Community-maintained packages are available for Debian (>= 13), Ubuntu (>= 22.10), Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch. day.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
day.readme: MuJoCo stands for Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind. MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers.

day.description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
day.readme: Claude Quickstarts is a collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building applications using the Claude API. Each quickstart provides a foundation that you can easily build upon and customize for your specific needs. To use these quickstarts, you'll need an Claude API key. If you don't have one yet, you can sign up for free at console.anthropic.com. A customer support agent powered by Claude.

Give the agent you already use a memory you control. GBrain stores explicit facts with their sources, supports corrections and withdrawal, and makes the same memory available across your agents. Start with keyless memory and keyword retrieval; add semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment when you need them. GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host; gbrain.io is optional paid hosting. Keep skills beside knowledge. New local brains include memory skills in their content root.

day.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
day.readme: Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

week.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.

week.readme: Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.

week.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
week.readme: Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

week.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

week.readme: Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio. 49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team. Building a game solo with AI is powerful, but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" Claude Code Game Studios solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio.

items.title: Maintenance agencies can price routine fixes using measured costs after repository learning
items.connection: The harness comparison motivates measuring cost per solved task, while Microsoft's economizer provides repository lesson reuse that could change those costs after repeated work.
items.context: Fixed-price maintenance loses margin when agents repeatedly rediscover build commands and repository conventions.
chain: The reported comparison shows similar coding pass rates can hide different costs.
Repository lesson reuse may reduce repeated failures as an engagement continues.
Agencies can benchmark both fresh and experienced sessions before choosing a workflow.
Stable routine-task costs could support prepaid maintenance packages for smaller clients.
items.who: Small software clients benefit; maintenance agencies would fund the tooling.
items.variable: Gross margin per accepted maintenance fix
items.versus: Measured costs after repeated repository work provide a stronger pricing basis than choosing a harness by reputation or introductory performance.
items.smallest_test: Compare compatible setups on 20 representative fixes with and without repository lessons; succeed if one lowers cost per accepted fix by 15% without increasing reviewer time.
items.disconfirm: Savings disappear after review and failed attempts are counted, or the plugin cannot operate in the candidate setups.

items.title: Warehouse teams can turn spoken stock questions into reviewable database queries
items.connection: Wllama supplies browser-local speech interaction, while Auto Ontology supplies business schemas for a custom text-to-SQL workflow that shows its interpretation before execution.
items.context: Warehouse staff often need answers while their hands are occupied; database access still needs permission controls.
chain: Browser-local speech provides an alternative to typing inventory questions.
A schema-guided query layer maps the transcript to business terms and requests confirmation.
Read-only execution can answer routine questions without an analyst translating each request.
Analysts can spend more time investigating discrepancies instead of retrieving stock counts.
items.who: Warehouse supervisors benefit; distribution operators would pay.
items.versus: A narrow voice interface could fit an existing inventory database more closely than a general assistant, provided query validation works.
items.smallest_test: Build a read-only prototype for one stock table and test 20 spoken questions; succeed if at least 18 produce the correct answer and every ambiguous request asks for clarification.
items.disconfirm: Speech errors or schema ambiguity routinely produce plausible but incorrect answers after confirmation.

items.title: Software buyers can request reproducible vulnerability evidence before demanding supplier fixes
items.connection: Hermes can identify, verify and export security findings, while Cloudflare Sandboxes offers an execution environment for a custom step that runs candidate reproductions.
items.context: Supplier security disputes often stall when buyers send findings that suppliers cannot reproduce.
chain: Hermes connects repository investigation with candidate verification and reporting.
A separate adapter can run suitable reproduction code in a sandbox using synthetic data.
Buyers can attach observed behavior and reproduction instructions to remediation requests.
Supplier discussions can focus on demonstrable defects rather than competing severity claims.
items.who: Procurement security teams and suppliers benefit; enterprise software buyers would pay.
items.variable: Time from reported finding to supplier acknowledgment
items.versus: A reproducible evidence packet could reduce dispute time compared with forwarding an unverified scanner report.
items.smallest_test: Use an authorized test repository with five seeded flaws; succeed if three yield independently repeatable sandbox reproductions and no unverified candidate is labeled confirmed.
items.disconfirm: The important flaws depend on production conditions the sandbox cannot represent, or independent reviewers cannot reproduce the reported behavior.

items.title: Facilities vendors can test economical monitoring before committing to edge hardware
items.connection: Omarchy's packaged local runtimes can reduce setup work for a prototype following the Strands guide's local-to-cloud routing pattern.
items.context: Facilities teams receive repetitive equipment alerts, while hardware purchases are harder to reverse than software trials.
chain: Packaged model recipes reduce the work needed to assemble a local trial.

Recorded alerts can reveal which tasks actually need cloud reasoning.
Vendors can size hardware and price monitoring services using observed escalation demand.
items.who: Facilities operators benefit; building maintenance and monitoring vendors would pay.
items.variable: Cloud cost per correctly triaged alert
items.versus: A software-first replay test can expose weak economics before buying edge hardware or sending every alert to a cloud model.
items.smallest_test: Replay 100 labeled equipment alerts through a compatible prototype; succeed if cloud calls fall by 30%, critical-alert recall matches the cloud-only baseline, and latency meets the operator's limit.

items.title: Career services can reduce repeat revisions without sharing applicants' personal histories
items.connection: The forkable job-search workflow supplies posting evaluation and application drafting, while Evolver could retain adviser-approved process lessons separately from applicant-specific content.
items.context: Career advisers repeatedly correct generic application mistakes, but personal details should stay specific to each applicant.
chain: The existing workflow packages common application tasks.
Advisers can approve general lessons from corrections and exclude personal facts.
Later applications can retrieve relevant process guidance while using only the current applicant's evidence.
Career services can spend less time fixing repeated drafting mistakes and more time on individual positioning.

items.lead: Large models are becoming accessible through more local hardware and runtime choices.
items.body: Llama-modchip reports running 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM without a GPU, while Omarchy users can select packaged TensorFold recipes for local models. These offer builders more hardware options and less setup work for local agents. Neither supplies performance comparisons, and Llama-modchip provides no speed or quality measurements.

items.lead: Agent tools are turning lessons from earlier work into reusable knowledge that may improve success and reduce costs.
items.body: Evolver stores and retrieves structured lessons without changing model weights; across 320 paired runs, reported success rose from 83.13% to 87.50% while recorded token use fell 24.24%. Microsoft's free token economizer plugin remembers repository knowledge from coding-agent sessions, with reported cost reductions of 18 to 31% in its tests. Builders can use these tools to reduce repeated discovery and failed commands, but the measured benefits remain limited to the reported tests.
